heroHeadline: PM Tells Special UN Meeting Haitians 'Can Wait No Longer' as GSF Mandate Renewal Vote Nears
heroSubtitle: A September 16, 2026 RNDDH report (widely covered September 17-18) consolidated two Kenscoff gang attacks into a combined toll of at least 164 killed, 23 injured and 71 kidnapped, faulting police "passivity" and a roughly 60% withdrawal of specialized Kenscoff units during 2026 for failing to prevent the violence. The Haitian National Police responded with a multi-day operation in Kenscoff beginning September 16, which the commune's mayor said had made "advances on the ground," though no arrests or casualties were reported. On September 24, Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé addressed a special UN meeting on Haiti's security and elections, saying "there is a people who can wait no longer" and confirming general elections remain on track for December 13, 2026 with electoral operations underway. The meeting underscored how thin the Gang Suppression Force remains ahead of a Security Council vote expected before its September 30 mandate expiration: just 1,083 personnel are deployed against the 5,500-person authorized ceiling, while 6.4 million Haitians need humanitarian assistance and nearly 1.5 million remain displaced. The GSF has formally requested a two-year extension through September 2028.
